headline: MEA condemns, attacker still unattributed
dek: The vessel struck off Lima, Oman on Monday evening is the India-flagged MSV AL JUSUFI, carrying 14 Indian seafarers. It was hit by an 'unidentified aerial object'.
sources: India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) statement, Tuesday 2026-11-03, and Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal's statement
fault_line: Who struck the AL JUSUFI off Lima -- and why does no government name the attacker while seafarers keep dying?

sections.what_happened: The vessel struck off Lima, Oman on Monday evening is the India-flagged MSV AL JUSUFI, carrying 14 Indian seafarers. It was hit by an 'unidentified aerial object'. 13 crew were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard; one seafarer, Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, died of his injuries. The MEA condemned the attack and reiterated its call for de-escalation and for protection of commercial shipping; the Indian Embassy in Oman is coordinating repatriation of the rescued crew and the mortal remains. NO attacker is named by the MEA, the minister, or the outlets carrying the statement. This is a casualty/identity update to the 0000-01 UKMTO incident, NOT a second strike: the initial UKMTO-linked report said vessel and crew safe, which is reconciled here as injuries proving fatal after the initial report, not as a separate event. The October 11 MT Petro Dolphin attack off Sohar (2 Indian seafarers missing) is a SEPARATE incident and is not merged into this toll.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct declared-tier families: MEA itself (T1 national-officials lane, STATE IN) for its own statement, and The Hindu (T2). Khaleej Times, The Statesman, Telegraph India, DD India and ABP Live carry the same MEA statement but hold NO declared tier in the registry and are reported with attribution only, never counted. The IANS-carried version (AsiaPost) is likewise uncounted: IANS has no registry row (ANI is T1; IANS is not ANI). Passes the sig-3 gate (>=2 families).
sections.what_disputed: UKMTO Warning 193-26's initial master's report (0000-01) said vessel and crew safe -- superseded in outcome by the MEA death report, not a contradiction of a separate event. No Saudi, Omani, US or CENTCOM attribution of the Lima strike surfaced in-window. Ansar Allah has not been linked to this strike by any counted source; do not attribute it to them.
sections.why_matters: The Hormuz strike now has a name and a face: Gujarat sailor Gandhar Nahim Ajij killed, 13 rescued -- and still no one says who fired. (First casualty in the Hormuz-mouth shipping war; claim-bust frame: name the dead, refuse the unattributed blame.)
